incoming.name: Canal
incoming.excerpt: The longest canal of ancient times was the Grand Canal of China.

incoming.name: Great Wall of China
incoming.excerpt: Astronaut William Pogue thought he had seen it from Skylab but discovered he was actually looking at the Grand Canal of China near Beijing.

incoming.name: Ibn Battuta
incoming.excerpt: He also travelled even further north, through the Grand Canal to Beijing, although there has been some doubt about whether this actually occurred.

incoming.name: Ming Dynasty
incoming.excerpt: Internally, the Grand Canal was expanded to its farthest limits and proved to be a stimulus to domestic trade.

outgoing.name: Confucius
outgoing.excerpt: This part is thought, on the strength of a passage in one of the books of Confucius, to have been built c. 486 BC.

outgoing.name: Marco Polo
outgoing.excerpt: Marco Polo recounted the Grand Canal's arched bridges as well as the warehouses and the prosperous trade in the 13th century.

outgoing.name: Ming Dynasty
outgoing.excerpt: The entire canal was reconstructed between 1411 and 1415 during the Ming Dynasty by the Yongle Emperor.
